# GitHub Copilot instructions

Repository-wide rules apply to implementation, refactoring, debugging, and pull request review. Read
`AGENTS.md` for architecture and every matching `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` file for
subsystem guidance.

## Non-negotiable rules

- Never edit, commit, or suggest changes to `main.js`; it is generated by the build.
- Preserve desktop and web extension-host behavior. Keep Windows, macOS, and Linux path, IPC, process,
  proxy, and shell behavior unless a change is explicitly platform-scoped.
- Preserve the published API, legacy compatibility API, command IDs, tree item IDs/context values,
  settings, and persisted state unless the change includes an intentional compatibility or migration
  plan.
- This extension is a generic host for other Azure extensions. Prefer shared Azure Tools abstractions
  and existing contribution/provider contracts over product-specific logic or direct SDK plumbing.
- Make the smallest complete change and avoid unrelated cleanup.
- Never expose access tokens, credentials, subscription or tenant secrets, connection strings, tag
  values, arbitrary file contents, or agent artifacts in logs, errors, telemetry, tree descriptions,
  diagnostics, or review output.
- Never emit telemetry containing arbitrary user input, resource names/IDs, user paths, prompts, or
  artifact contents. Record bounded booleans, enums, versions, counts, and known categories.
- Treat cross-extension contributions, tree models, API requests, workspace files, and Copilot-created
  artifacts as untrusted and potentially incomplete.

## Azure Tools conventions

### Commands, contexts, telemetry, and errors

- Register normal commands with `registerCommand` or `registerCommandWithTreeNodeUnwrapping` from
  `@microsoft/vscode-azext-utils`.
  - Use tree-node unwrapping when a command can receive an Azure Resources wrapper or multi-select
    arguments.
  - Use raw `vscode.commands.registerCommand` only for deliberate internal commands outside the Azure
    Tools action pipeline.
- Pass one `IActionContext` through the full operation. Do not create ad hoc telemetry, UI, or error
  contexts below the entry point.
- Use `callWithTelemetryAndErrorHandling` for activation work, provider callbacks, events, webview
  callbacks, API boundaries, and MCP tools.
  - Set `context.errorHandling.rethrow` when an API caller must observe rejection.
  - Suppress display only when another layer deliberately owns the user-facing error.
- Treat `UserCancelledError` and prompt cancellation as cancellation, not failure.
- Add user-controlled values that may appear in errors to `context.valuesToMask`, or use an existing
  masking helper.
- Catch only optional failures or errors translated into a more actionable failure. Record the bounded
  reason, then intentionally continue or rethrow.

### Wizards and activities

- Use `AzureWizard` for prompts, validation, conditional branches, or multiple durable side effects.
- Prompt steps collect and validate context and implement `shouldPrompt`; they must tolerate Back
  navigation and reruns without durable side effects.
- Execute steps perform durable work and implement `shouldExecute` so resumed or pre-populated flows do
  not repeat it. Execution order follows numeric `priority`, not array position.
- Compose existing Azure Tools prompt/execute steps before adding new ones.
- Azure mutations should use `createActivityContext`, useful `activityTitle` text, progress reporting,
  and the repository's Activity Log integration.
- Refresh the narrowest affected tree item after a long-running mutation completes.

### Azure clients, subscriptions, and resources

- Use `src/utils/azureClients.ts`, `src/services/**`, or shared Azure Tools factories. Do not instantiate
  extension-specific `@azure/arm-*` clients in feature code.
- Keep runtime Azure SDK imports lazy and module-scope SDK imports type-only where practical.
- Pass `IActionContext` with the correct subscription context to client factories; never copy
  credentials manually.
- Preserve sovereign/custom cloud behavior, complete paging with `uiUtils.listAllIterator`, partial SDK
  models, provider activation, and eventual consistency.
- Await long-running Azure operations with `begin...AndWait` unless returning early is an intentional,
  visible product behavior.

### Trees, providers, and compatibility

- Keep resource discovery, branch visualization, and tree orchestration separate:
  resource providers return resources; branch data providers own models; tree providers own grouping,
  wrapping, state, and refresh.
- Preserve lazy activation of contributing extensions. Do not eagerly activate every Azure extension.
- Keep item IDs stable and case-insensitive where the existing lookup path expects that. Context-value
  changes require checking all `package.json` `when` clauses and command pickers.
- Maintain `BranchDataItemCache`, `TreeItemStateStore`, grouping, load-more, narrow refresh, disposal,
  and Azure/Workspace/Focused/Tenant/Activity view behavior.
- Preserve v1 compatibility adapters and the current API together until an explicit removal plan says
  otherwise.
- Attach emitters, listeners, providers, controllers, and watchers to the owning disposable or
  `ext.context.subscriptions`.

### UI, files, processes, and localization

- Prefer `context.ui` inside action flows so cancellation, testing, and queued input work consistently.
- Localize every user-visible string with the nearby `localize(...)` or `vscode.l10n.t(...)` pattern;
  localize `package.json` contributions through `package.nls.json`.
- Use `vscode.workspace.fs`, `Uri`, and existing helpers in web-compatible paths. Isolate Node-only file,
  child-process, socket, and stream code to desktop-only subsystems.
- Use `path.join`/`Uri.joinPath` and existing path guards. Pass executables and arguments separately when
  possible; never interpolate user-controlled values into a shell command.
- Use existing webview controllers/lifecycle helpers rather than recreating panel plumbing.

## TypeScript and design

- Follow `@microsoft/eslint-config-azuretools` and strict `tsconfig.json` settings.
- Prefer type guards, discriminated unions, `import type`, and typed non-null helpers over `any`, broad
  assertions, duplicate interfaces, or silent coercion.
- Keep orchestration thin and put reusable logic in the existing owning module.
- Follow nearby naming, context, provider, step, factory, and controller patterns before inventing new
  ones.
- Keep activation light: avoid synchronous I/O, network work, broad extension activation, and expensive
  runtime imports at module load.
- Public API changes require source types, host implementation, version/compatibility review, generated
  API declarations, changelog/docs, and boundary tests.
- Command changes require contribution metadata, localized titles, registration, arguments, context
  values, and tests.
- Configuration changes require contribution metadata, constants/accessors, defaults/scopes, telemetry,
  and user documentation.

## Testing and validation

- Add focused deterministic regression coverage when practical; keep live Azure behavior behind the
  existing nightly gates.
- Use the test-only `99.0.0` API when behavior must cross the bundled extension boundary; never import
  `src/testApi.ts` from production code.
- Run the smallest relevant checks:
  - `npm run build:check` for TypeScript.
  - `npm run lint` for repository lint and agent-drift rules.
  - `npm run build` for bundling, activation/import changes, Cloud Shell child-process code, webviews, or
    package behavior.
  - `npm test` for extension integration behavior; use the existing VS Code test filtering for focused
    tests.
  - `npm run api-extractor` for published `api/` changes.
- Documentation-only changes need no build unless a repository check validates the changed documents.

## Pull request review

Review concrete correctness, reliability, compatibility, security, and user-facing regressions. Skip
formatting enforced by TypeScript, ESLint, or build tools.

For each changed flow, verify:

- Contribution/API -> registration -> provider/handler -> result and narrow refresh.
- Command arguments across palette, tree menu, multi-select, API, and MCP/programmatic calls.
- Provider registration/disposal, lazy extension activation, item IDs/context values, cache/state, load
  more, grouping, and every affected view.
- Correct subscription/tenant/custom-cloud context, complete paging/LRO behavior, and no customer-data
  leakage.
- Desktop/web and Windows/macOS/Linux behavior for files, IPC, child processes, sockets, and proxies.
- Public APIs, auth sessions, compatibility adapters, settings, command IDs, stored state, and telemetry.
- Wizard Back/cancel behavior, destructive confirmation, activity output, and actionable errors.
- Copilot artifact validation, approval gates, handoffs, resume state, docs, and focused regression tests.
- `main.js` remains untouched.

Report only findings that have a concrete triggering scenario and observable impact. Include the
file/line, severity, failure mode, and smallest viable fix. Verify assumptions against local code and
relevant `microsoft/vscode-azuretools` behavior.

Keep every review comment clear, concise, and ELI5. By default, use two or three short sentences:
what action or input triggers the problem, what the user will see, and how to fix it. Prefer plain words,
define unavoidable jargon, and do not bury the finding in background detail. Give a longer explanation
only when the reviewer asks for one.
